body.text: Nothing disrupts a medical trip faster than flying across time zones only to discover an untreated anaemia, high blood sugar, or heart rhythm irregularity on the morning of surgery. [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) is an independent, client-paid, flat-fee travel and medical travel advisory run by its two founders in Türkiye—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions. We build realistic arrival buffers and flexible bookings around the clinical clearance process run by your licensed hospital team.
Which tests (CBC, coagulation, HbA1c, infectious panel, ECG) are done on arrival?

On Day 1 in Türkiye, most surgical hospitals run a fast-turnaround laboratory panel covering Complete Blood Count (CBC), clotting times (PT, INR, aPTT), kidney and liver function, electrolytes, blood glucose or HbA1c, viral serology (HIV, Hepatitis B and C), and a resting 12-lead ECG, with chest imaging added when clinically indicated.

International clinical standards such as the [NICE Guideline NG45 on Routine Preoperative Tests for Elective Surgery](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng45) outline how testing—including [full blood count, resting ECG, and HbA1c](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng45/chapter/recommendations)—is tailored to surgery complexity and patient health status. Turkish hospitals still repeat core blood work in-house before general anaesthesia so their anaesthesiologists rely on fresh, same-day values processed by their own accredited laboratory.

body.text: When is it smarter to run baseline labs at home before booking flights?

It is smarter to run baseline blood tests and a GP check at home four to six weeks before booking flights if you have diabetes, hypertension, thyroid disease, anaemia, a history of blood clots, a BMI over 35, or take daily prescription medications—especially blood thinners or GLP-1 weight-loss drugs.

The [U.S. Embassy in Türkiye](https://tr.usembassy.gov/medical-tourism/) specifically advises obtaining a medical evaluation from a home doctor four to six weeks prior to travelling for elective surgery. Similarly, [NICE's Tests Before Surgery patient guide](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng45/resources/tests-before-surgery-pdf-3141108622789) recommends that patients with diagnosed diabetes have an HbA1c result taken within the previous three months before surgery. Catching low iron or elevated HbA1c at home gives your doctor time to treat it safely before you pay for flights or hotel nights.
What abnormal results can postpone or cancel surgery safely?

Anaesthesiologists and surgeons may safely postpone or cancel elective surgery if arrival tests reveal severe anaemia (low haemoglobin), uncontrolled blood sugar or high HbA1c, abnormal clotting times, newly detected cardiac arrhythmias on ECG, active respiratory infection, or a positive pregnancy test.

A cancellation in Istanbul feels frustrating, yet it is a sign of a responsible clinical team putting patient safety above revenue. Through our [medical tourism coordination service](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism), we always recommend refundable hotel tiers and changeable flight fares so an unexpected medical deferral does not compound into a major financial loss.
Pre-Departure Medical Clearance & Travel Prep Checklist:

items: Book a home GP check 4–6 weeks out: Run a baseline CBC, metabolic panel, and HbA1c if you have any chronic condition or prior surgical risk.
Review medication pauses with your doctors: Never stop blood thinners, diabetes drugs, or blood pressure pills on your own; obtain written instructions from both your home doctor and surgical team.
Keep a clean medication list: Carry an English list of exact drug names, dosages, and allergies for your Day 1 anaesthesia interview.

Verify facility authorization: Check that your hospital holds a valid license on the [Turkish Ministry of Health authorized providers list](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html).
Plan a fasting arrival window: Confirm how many hours before your Day 1 blood draw you must avoid food and caffeine.

body.text: Are pre-op labs included in hospital quotes?

Standard Day 1 blood panels and a basic resting ECG are usually included in written hospital surgical quotes in Türkiye, whereas extra specialist consultations—such as a cardiology echocardiogram, pulmonology clearance, sleep study, or corrective IV iron infusion triggered by abnormal findings—are typically billed separately.

Before paying a deposit, ask your hospital's international patient coordinator for an itemized written list showing which diagnostics are bundled and what unit fees apply if the anaesthesiologist orders additional imaging or specialist sign-off. Transparent line items prevent billing surprises on Day 1.

faq.q: If I bring recent blood test results from home, will the Turkish hospital skip Day 1 labs?
faq.a: Usually no. Home labs are valuable for pre-travel screening and spotting issues early, but Turkish anaesthesiologists typically require fresh in-house blood work and an ECG on arrival before administering general anaesthesia.

faq.q: Do I need to fast before my arrival blood tests in Türkiye?
faq.a: In most cases, yes—hospitals commonly request 8 to 12 hours of fasting (with plain water allowed only if approved) for accurate glucose and metabolic readings. Confirm exact fasting rules with your clinical team before your flight.

faq.q: How fast do Day 1 lab results come back in Istanbul hospitals?
faq.a: Large private hospitals run on-site laboratories, so routine CBC, clotting, biochemistry, and serology panels usually return within two to four hours, allowing afternoon surgical clearance or next-morning operations.

faq.q: What happens if I have a cold or fever right before flying to Türkiye?
faq.a: Notify your licensed surgical team immediately before boarding. Active respiratory infections or fever increase general anaesthesia airway risks and often require rescheduling until you fully recover.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye review my blood tests or give medical clearance?
faq.a: No. Learn more [about Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about): we are an independent, client-paid, flat-fee travel advisory run by two founders in Türkiye. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.

faq.q: Should I carry printed copies of my home medical records?
faq.a: Yes. Keep printed English summaries of chronic conditions, recent ECGs, and prescription lists in your cabin bag for your in-person anaesthesia assessment, without sending sensitive files prematurely during early enquiries.
